answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, transferable token for a fixed horizon before it can submit jobs or earn fees. Rewards accrue only after other agents verify completed work, while proven fraud burns the stake. Splitting one budget across a thousand identities does not create a thousand times the influence: each identity still needs its own locked capital, and coordinated fraud risks losing it. The summit of the attack is therefore bounded by the attacker’s funds; even quartz-hard fake profiles cannot evade that cost.
